name: People's Republic of China

areaKm2.note: world_1960 China polygon = ~8.20M km2 computed on the sphere (low; the basemap polygon omits some western territory). Official PRC area ~9.6M km2 (mid/high). Excludes Taiwan.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1979 = 985,467k (high). OWID population CSV China 1979 = 969.3M (low). Official year-end 1979 figure ~975M used as mid (from memory).

urbanization.note: OWID urban share China 1979 = 19.1%. Low = COW upop/tpop = 129.4M/985.5M = 0.13 (large cities only).

activePersonnel.note: COW NMC v7 milper 1979 = 4,600k (high). Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80, Table II-1: Army strength 3,600,000 (main forces 115 infantry, 11 armoured, 40 artillery and 16 railway divisions; local forces 85 infantry divisions). Navy ~0.3M and Air Force ~0.4M added for the mid.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: armed (core) militia with basic weapons training; the ordinary militia of tens of millions is untrained and sits in mobilizable. Western estimates of the armed militia in the late 1970s were ~5-7M (IISS, not fetched).

supportPersonnel.note: Active minus P roles: Navy, Air Force, Second Artillery, artillery, armour, AAA, engineer and railway divisions, logistics and staff (4.3M - ~1.35M infantry).

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess: people's war doctrine with a huge militia; Korean War and civil-war peaks were ~5-6M under arms of ~550M (~0.01), so the total-war ratio is a judgement.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Infantry of 115 main-force infantry divisions (~12,000 men, ~60% infantry = ~7,000 each, ~800,000) plus 85 local-force infantry divisions at lower strength (~5,000 infantry each, ~425,000); division counts from Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Type 56 rifles and RPG-2/Type 69, 57-82 mm recoilless rifles; Yang: anti-tank weapons years behind the Soviets

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Cultural Revolution disrupted training; no combat since 1969; human-wave tactics and heavy losses in Feb 1979

count.note: Educated guess: 15th Airborne Corps (3 divisions, ~30,000), independent main-force regiments (150, part infantry) and border/mountain units. Cavalry divisions were converted in the 1970s and are not counted separately.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: light weapons only

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: airborne relatively better trained

count.note: Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80: 16,000-18,000 field guns and howitzers (122, 130, 152 mm) plus a few SP guns (SU-76/85/100, ISU-122); high adds 107/130 mm MRLs. Mortars excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Soviet 1950s designs (D-30 copies came later), towed, no modern fire control

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: massed preparatory barrages effective at Lang Son 1979

count.note: Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80: Table II-1 11,000 tanks (IS-2, T-34, Type 59 medium, Type 62 light, Type 63 amphibious); text gives some 10,000. Sino-Vietnamese War article: 400-550 tanks committed to Vietnam (200 Type 59/62/63 in the first wave).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Type 59 = T-54A copy without stabiliser or rangefinder, a generation behind the T-72 (Yang)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: weak infantry-tank cooperation in Vietnam 1979, heavy tank losses

count.note: Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80: Table II-1 1,500 K-63 (Type 63) APCs; text gives 3,500 Chinese-designed APCs. Mid splits the two.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Type 63 tracked APC, no IFVs

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: little mechanised doctrine

count.note: Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80, Table II-2: MiG-15 500, MiG-17 and MiG-19 (J-5/J-6) 3,700, MiG-21 80; ~300-500 of the MiG-19 family are Q-5 attack aircraft counted in strike. PLAAF article: 50 air divisions in 1971-89. Naval aviation fighters (~500) partly added in the high.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: J-6 (MiG-19) and J-5 (MiG-17) a generation behind MiG-23/F-15; Chinese MiG-21s nearly all grounded by 1975 (Yang)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: PLAAF article: Cultural Revolution closed technical schools and damaged pilot training; PLAAF largely stayed out of the 1979 war

count.note: Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80, Table II-2: Tu-16 (H-6) 80-90, Il-28 (H-5) 300, Tu-2 100 = ~480; plus ~300 Q-5 attack aircraft inside the MiG-19 family total and naval aviation Il-28s (high).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: Il-28 (1947 design), Tu-2 piston bombers still in service

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: see fighters

count.note: Educated guess: Z-5 (Mi-4 copy), Mi-8, Z-6, Alouette III and Super Frelon in Army and Navy service; small transport force.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: piston Z-5 dominant

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: little airmobile experience

count.note: Educated guess: about 11 destroyers (4 ex-Soviet Anshan class, ~7 Type 051 Luda) and ~16 frigates (Jiangdong, Jianghu, Chengdu, Jiangnan); Yang only says handfuls of destroyers and frigates.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Luda (1971) with Styx copies, no SAMs, poor sensors

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: coastal navy, little blue-water experience

count.note: Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80: 160 Osa/Hola/Komar missile boats, 403 fast attack gunboats, 220 torpedo boats and over 120 hydrofoil torpedo boats = 903. PLAN article: missile-carrying ships grew from 20 to 200 in the 1970s.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Styx-armed FACs dangerous near the coast, vulnerable to ECM (Yang)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: coastal people's-war navy

count.note: Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80: some 91 medium-range torpedo attack submarines (Romeo/Whiskey types), 1 Han-class nuclear submarine and 1 Golf-class SSB without missiles = 93. PLAN article: conventional submarines grew from 35 to 100 in the 1970s.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: Romeo (Type 033) a 1950s design; Han SSN noisy and unreliable

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: short-range patrols only

count.note: Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80, Table II-4: 2 CSS-3 (DF-4) ICBM, 50-70 CSS-2 (DF-3) IRBM, 40-50 CSS-1 (DF-2) MRBM launchers.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: liquid-fuelled, slow to launch, inaccurate; DF-5 ICBM first full test May 1980

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Second Artillery an elite, politically trusted service

count.note: Batteries. Yang, The Modernization of the Chinese PLA (Naval Postgraduate School thesis, June 1980, DTIC ADA092422), tables citing the IISS Military Balance 1979-80: ~10,000 anti-aircraft guns (14.5-100 mm) at ~6 per battery = ~1,650, plus ~100 HQ-2/CSA-1 (SA-2) SAM launchers at ~6 per site = ~17 sites.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25. Evidence: guns and late-1950s SA-2 copies only, no mobile SAMs (Yang)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: large dedicated AAA divisions, Vietnam War experience 1965-69

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: military ranks abolished 1965-88, Cultural Revolution purges; 1979 offensive showed poor coordination, weak communications and logistics

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5. Evidence: national conscript and volunteer army with strong political-commissar system

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5-0.75. Evidence: nationalist campaign to punish Vietnam; heavy losses (6,954-8,531 killed in about a month, Sino-Vietnamese War article)

weapons.note: Anchor: weapons 8 (1943: tanks, dive bombers, radar-directed AA). Evidence: Type 59 tank, towed 1950s artillery, J-6 jets, Styx-copy anti-ship missiles; well short of the 1985 anchor

armor.note: Anchor: armor 8 (rolled homogeneous armour). Evidence: Type 59 and Type 63 cast/rolled steel, no composite armour

ships.note: Anchor: ships 8 (carriers, radar, submarines) to 9. Evidence: Luda destroyers, Romeo submarines, one Han SSN; no carriers

fortification.note: Anchor: fortification 8 (concrete lines). Evidence: "Underground Great Wall" tunnel and bunker networks against Soviet invasion

logistics.note: Anchor: logistics between 7 (railways) and 8 (motor transport). Evidence: rail to the border, then trucks and civilian porters; 1979 advance stalled by supply

communications.note: Anchor: communications 8 (radio at company level). Evidence: radio below regiment scarce, poor tactical comms in 1979

isr.note: Anchor: isr 8 (radar) to 9 (satellites). Evidence: early-warning radars; FSW recoverable reconnaissance satellites from 1975

air.note: Anchor: air 8 (1943) to 9 (1985). Evidence: J-6 supersonic (MiG-19, 1955 design), H-6 (Tu-16); a generation behind

cyber.note: No military computer networks before ~1985 (cyber 9 anchor = 1990 networks).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: official 1979 defence budget ~22bn yuan (~5-6% of GNP, raised for the Vietnam war); Western estimates of real spending higher. Wartime year: low is roughly the 1978 peacetime share.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: industry ~45% of GDP in 1979 under the Soviet-model heavy-industry strategy, but most of the workforce in farming.

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of the labour force (share of food output not eaten by the farm population; no calorie self-sufficiency adjustment). World Bank WDI Database Archives (version 1999 Apr), SL.AGR.TOTL.ZS "Labor force in agriculture (% of total)" (ILO-based) China 1979 = 74.7% (1980 = 74.2%). CIA World Factbook 1990: 61.1% (1986), after decollectivisation. Share 74.7% (range 71.0-78.0%) -> 0.253 (0.22-0.29).

annualCohort.note: Educated guess: males reaching 18 in 1979 = born 1961, the Great Leap famine birth trough (~12M births); adjacent cohorts are larger.

artillery.note: Educated guess: towed guns and MRLs; China was a large artillery producer.

armor.note: Educated guess: Type 59/62/63 output at Baotou (Factory 617) in the late 1970s.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess: J-6 production at Shenyang (~5,000 built 1958-81 incl. exports) and J-7 start.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess: Q-5 (Nanchang) and H-6/H-5 output.

helicopters.note: Educated guess: Z-5 production ended 1979; small Z-9 licence programme from 1980.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: Luda destroyers and Jianghu frigates completed per year.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess: FAC and patrol boat output.

submarines.note: Educated guess: Type 033 Romeo (84 built 1962-84) and Ming class.

missiles.note: Educated guess: DF-2/DF-3 launchers per year.

air_defense.note: Educated guess: AAA batteries equipped per year.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: total highways ~875,000 km in 1979, mostly unsurfaced; paved or engineered all-weather share used here.

railKm.note: Educated guess: operating railway ~50,000 km in 1979, single-track to the Vietnamese border at Pingxiang and Hekou.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Shanghai, Dalian, Tianjin (Xingang), Qingdao, Guangzhou (Huangpu), Zhanjiang, Qinhuangdao, Lianyungang, Ningbo, Fuzhou, Xiamen, Yantai, Shantou, Beihai.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: COSCO and provincial fleets ~7M dwt in 1979, fast-growing.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: PLA logistics in 1979 relied on rail to the border and porters/trucks; the offensive reached only 15-40 km into Vietnam (Sino-Vietnamese War article).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses (~11M), mules, donkeys and draft cattle/buffalo in the late 1970s.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS estimate (Kristensen and Korda, via OWID nuclear-warhead-stockpiles CSV) China 1979 = 195 warheads; range for Norris and Kristensen variants.

homeDefense.note: 1.3 row: huge strategic depth, harsh mountain and desert frontiers, people's war doctrine with militia and tunnel defences.

notes: Snapshot date 17 February 1979, start of the Sino-Vietnamese War. Forces are national totals; the invasion force was ~200,000 troops with 400-550 tanks (Sino-Vietnamese War article, Chinese data), while ~1M troops faced the USSR. Key order-of-battle numbers come from a 1980 Naval Postgraduate School thesis (Yang, DTIC ADA092422, archive.org full text) whose tables cite the IISS Military Balance 1979-80. Population convention: mainland PRC, Taiwan excluded. Militia: armed core militia counted as trainedReserves; the ordinary militia falls under mobilizable. Many economic and logistics values are educated guesses (grade D) because no fetchable 1979 statistical yearbook was available.
